record.paper_title: Polycyclic Codes Associated with Trinomials: Good Codes and Open Questions
record.original_question: Over the binary field F_2, let C be a polycyclic code associated with the trinomial x^n - a x^i - b and generated by a divisor g(x) of that trinomial. Is C iso-dual if and only if g(x)^2 = x^n - a x^i - b?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2. Over F2, a polycyclic code C generated by g(x)|x^n - axi - b is iso-dual if and only if g^2(x) = x^n - axi - b.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the binary field $\mathbb{F}_2$. Fix integers $n\ge 2$ and $0<i<n$, and elements $a,b\in\mathbb{F}_2$ with $b\ne 0$, so that $f(x)=x^n-ax^i-b\in\mathbb{F}_2[x]$ is a trinomial. For a monic divisor $g(x)\mid f(x)$ in $\mathbb{F}_2[x]$ of degree $k$, the polycyclic code $C$ associated with $f$ and generated by $g$ is
$$C=\{g(x)\,h(x)\bmod f(x):h(x)\in\mathbb{F}_2[x]/(f(x))\}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^n,$$
identifying polynomials of degree $<n$ with their coefficient vectors. The Euclidean dual $C^\perp$ is taken with respect to the standard inner product on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The code $C$ is called iso-dual if $C$ is monomially (equivalently, permutation, over $\mathbb{F}_2$) equivalent to $C^\perp$.

Prove or disprove: $C$ is iso-dual if and only if $g(x)^2=x^n-ax^i-b$.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is posed as a conjecture in the work introducing polycyclic codes from trinomials, published in Designs, Codes and Cryptography (2022). Subsequent literature on polycyclic codes (duality, isodual constructions from polycirculant matrices, skew polycyclic codes, and polycyclic codes over finite chain rings) discusses the framework but does not appear to settle this specific binary characterization, so it remains open.

status_evidence.title: Polycyclic codes associated with trinomials: good codes and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Several conjectures about polynomials and polycyclic codes have been stated, including conjectures related to their equivalence and duality.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectured binary iso-duality characterization is stated as an open question in this published work.

status_evidence.title: On polycyclic linear and additive codes associated to a trinomial over a finite chain ring
status_evidence.snippet: Extends polycyclic codes associated with trinomials to finite chain rings, discussing equivalence and duality.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work continues to investigate duality but does not resolve the binary iso-dual conjecture.
